lines.narration: Twinkie, his one friend here in the red beanie, spells it out: that spiky-haired man is Yakuza, actual mafia. Sean hears the word and takes it as a dare.

claim.subject: the friend in the red beanie

lines.narration: He calls the man out anyway. The spiky-haired man in the leather jacket breaks from the crowd and stops with his face an inch from Sean's. Neither backs off. Two words close it. Let's race.

claim.subject: the spiky-haired man in the leather jacket

lines.narration: The crowd asks with what — his skateboard — and a voice from the back says take mine. That is Han, who runs his own garage, handing a kid he's never met a car he built from the block up just to see what he's got.

claim.subject: the blond-dyed man in the leather jacket

lines.narration: In the lift Twinkie asks if he even knows what DK stands for. Sean guesses Donkey Kong. It's Drift King — not a nickname, a job title, and nobody in Tokyo races it for fun.

claim.subject: the friend in the red beanie

lines.narration: Twinkie's valuation of the borrowed car: it's the Mona Lisa of drift work. He sells sneakers out of a backpack — of course it's the Mona Lisa.

claim.subject: the friend in the red beanie

lines.narration: Sean drops into the seat and gets his whole drift education in thirty seconds: rip the e-brake to loosen the back end, then power over and hold it. That's the entire curriculum. He's never drifted in his life — and he's about to try it against the best driver in the city.

claim.subject: the friend in the red beanie

lines.narration: Before the start the man in the black tank top pulls the dark-haired woman into him in front of everyone and holds it, letting the garage watch. Her name is Neela, and he's claiming her as his.
The cars settle side by side, a man in a dark suit drops his arm, and they break away into the deck in tyre smoke.
Then he gets greedy on a corner, the tail goes further than he meant, and Han's car lays a line of sparks down the concrete. Twenty seconds in, he's already wrecked the one thing he was lent.
The man in the black tank top takes the identical corner broadside and makes it look like the corner was built for him. That contrast is the whole race.
He has the spiral ramps to himself and drops down them sideways, bursting out onto the neon street first while the crowd erupts for him.
In all that noise, two people aren't cheering. Twinkie, and Neela beside him, watching the exit with nothing on their faces at all.

Sean's car slides out dead last, front end torn open and smoking. The barrier breaks and the crowd swarms the wreck. He's lost in front of hundreds who all know exactly what that repair bill looks like.
A long-haired man in a grey jacket leans into his window to tell him what he already knows: barely a week in Tokyo and he owes a stranger an entire car.
He slips home after midnight to find the grey-haired man in the navy hoodie — his father — waiting in the dark with a beer.
His father is on his feet now, and the question is flat. Have you been racing, Sean.

claim.subject: the grey-haired man in the NAVY hoodie

lines.narration: Sean lifts a car key off the desk and heads for the door. His father corners him in the back room: there's nowhere else to send him. If this doesn't work out, he goes to jail — live by these rules, or get out. Sean has heard this speech in every town. This is the first one with a cell at the end of it.

claim.subject: the grey-haired man in the NAVY hoodie

lines.narration: Next day the long-haired man in the parka waits outside school to collect for the wrecked car. Sean says he'll get him his money. The man asks why he's talking like he has a choice — and drives him off to work as his delivery runner.

claim.subject: the long-haired man in the parka

lines.narration: He explains the job on the drive. A guy owes him money, and Sean is the one going in to collect. Sean doesn't ask a single question about what collecting means.

claim.subject: the long-haired man in the parka

lines.narration: The place is a bathhouse; the debtor, a mountain of a man with a wolf inked across his back, soaking in the pool. Sean leans on him in a towel and gets hurled into the street — goes back in, gets hurled out again, one shoe short.

On the night drive they strike the deal. Sean stays on call — once a week or once an hour, sick as a dog or in bed with Beyonce, the man calls and Sean shows. Only if you teach me to drift, Sean says. This isn't a negotiation. I wasn't negotiating, Sean says back.

claim.subject: the long-haired man in the dark jacket
